claims.statement: The order lifecycle is defined only by six `public static final String` constants on `OrderService` — `waitPay`, `waitDelivery`, `waitConfirm`, `waitReview`, `finish`, `delete`, each equal to its own identifier — while `Order.status` is a nullable `varchar(255)` column declared with no CHECK, ENUM or NOT NULL constraint, so there is no state-machine object, status enum or database-level validation of the legal values.

Exactly six call sites ever write `Order.status`: `ForeAction.createOrder` sets `waitPay`, `ForeAction.payed` sets `waitDelivery`, `ForeAction.orderConfirmed` sets `waitReview`, `ForeAction.deleteOrder` sets `delete`, `ForeAction.doreview` sets `finish`, and `OrderAction.delivery` sets `waitConfirm`; no action, service or interceptor restores or reverts a previous status.

Each transition stamps its own dedicated column and none of them clears a previously set value: `createOrder` writes `orderCode` (generated with `SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS")`) and `createDate`, `forepayed` writes `payDate`, `admin_order_delivery` writes `deliveryDate`, and `foreorderConfirmed` writes `confirmDate`.

`forecreateOrder` creates the order from the session's `orderItems` list written by `forebuy`: it returns `login.jsp` when that list is empty (and throws when the session key is absent, because the guard dereferences it), sets `orderCode`, `createDate`, the session `user` and `status = waitPay`, then overwrites the action's `total` with the value returned by the service and redirects to `forealipay?order.id=${order.id}&total=${total}`.

`OrderServiceImpl.createOrder` is the create composite write, annotated `@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRED, rollbackForClassName = "Exception")`: it saves the order, then for every `OrderItem` sets the parent order and calls `orderItemService.update(oi)`, accumulating and returning `promotePrice * number`. The internal `save(order)` is a self-invocation with no separate boundary, while the `OrderItemService` calls leave the object through the injected bean proxy and join the same transaction.

`ReviewServiceImpl.saveReviewAndUpdateOrderStatus` is the review composite write, annotated `@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRED, rollbackForClassName = "Exception")`, and it updates the order before inserting the `Review`, so the `finish` status change and the new review row commit or roll back as one unit.

`foredoreview` sets `status = finish`, HTML-escapes the posted `review.content` and stamps the review's product (from the form's hidden `product.id`), user (session user) and `createDate` before calling the service; the review screen itself offers only the first order item's product, because `forereview` selects it with `order.getOrderItems().get(0).getProduct()` after `orderItemService.fill(order)`.

Every transition other than creation begins with `t2p(order)`: the request contributes only `order.id`, and `Action4Service.t2p(Object)` re-reads the whole persisted row through `categoryService.get(clazz, id)` and reflects it back onto the action via the matching setter, so the subsequent status and timestamp writes land on persistent state rather than a partially bound object.

`foredeleteOrder` is a soft delete: it sets `status` to the `OrderService.delete` constant (a status value, not the inherited `BaseService.delete(Object)` row delete) and updates the row, leaving all order data in place, and it is instead the read path that hides it — `OrderService.listByUserWithoutDelete` combines `Restrictions.eq("user", user)` with `Restrictions.ne("status", OrderService.delete)`, whereas the admin list uses the unfiltered `listByPage`/`total()` and therefore still shows and counts soft-deleted orders.

The pay, ship, confirm and delete transitions are single-entity writes through `orderService.update(order)`; because `OrderServiceImpl` does not override `update`, the boundary is the inherited `ServiceDelegateDAO.update(Object)` annotated `@Transactional(readOnly = false)`, which opens its own transaction for each action-level call.

Transaction advice for the two composite writes is enabled by `<tx:annotation-driven transaction-manager="transactionManager"/>` against the Hibernate `HibernateTransactionManager`, making `createOrder` (Order + OrderItem) and `saveReviewAndUpdateOrderStatus` (Order + Review) the only order-lifecycle operations that write more than one entity atomically.

`Order.getStatusDesc()` maps the six status values to 待付, 待发, 待收, 等评, 完成 and 刪除 and falls back to 未知 otherwise; the admin order list renders it as `${o.statusDesc}` and gates its 发货 button on `${o.status=='waitDelivery'}`, and because the method switches on the raw status string, a row whose `status` is NULL (allowed by the nullable column) throws a NullPointerException during render.

`OrderItemServiceImpl.fill(Order)` decorates an order for rendering by reloading its items with `listByParent(order)`, summing `number * promotePrice` into the transient `total`, summing `number` into `totalNumber` and setting a first product image per item; because those fields are `@Transient` and recomputed from current rows, displayed totals can differ from the amount returned when the order was created, and the money formula is duplicated in `ForeAction.buy`, `OrderServiceImpl.createOrder` and `fill`.

Cart lines and order lines are the same `OrderItem` rows distinguished only by the `order` association: `orderItem.oid` is nullable and carries no foreign-key constraint, `createOrder` promotes an item by calling `oi.setOrder(order)`, and the cart's `foredeleteOrderItem` performs a hard `orderItemService.delete` on any posted `orderItem.id` without checking that the item is still an unattached cart line.

No transition action validates the order's current status or the acting user: the `fore*` transition endpoints are covered only by `AuthInterceptor`'s rule that a `/fore` URI requires a session `user` (the interceptor never compares that user with `order.user`), and `admin_order_delivery`, which performs the shipment transition, does not match the `/fore` prefix and is therefore outside the check entirely.

The buyer-facing 催卖家发货 button in the order list targets `admin_order_delivery?order.id=...` through an AJAX GET, so the buyer's own browser executes the `waitDelivery` → `waitConfirm` transition and stamps `deliveryDate` before any seller action; the admin 发货 button is rendered only for `waitDelivery` orders and is a presentation-only guard.

The session key `orderItems` is never cleared after `forecreateOrder`, and `OrderItem.order` is a single foreign key, so re-submitting the buy form runs `createOrder` again and re-points the same order items at a new order, leaving the earlier order with no order items.

`forealipay` writes nothing — it forwards to `alipay.jsp` — and the amount shown on the payment page comes from the URL parameter (`${param.total}`) rather than from the order, so the actual payment transition is a plain GET link to `forepayed` from that page.
No automated test covers any order transition: the repository's only test class exercises `Category`, and no test asserts a status value, a redirect target or a composite write.
